attributes.body:
One of the regular functions of と in Japanese is as a quotation particle. This use is called 引用（いんよう） in Japanese, which basically translates as 'reference', or 'citation'. This way of using と can appear after almost any type of word (or phrase), but requires だ when used after nouns or な-Adjectives.

と as a quotation marker will almost always be followed by a verb that shows what type of 'quote' it is. This can be words like 言（い）う, 思（おも）う, 考（かんが）える, 聞（き）く, etc. However, at the end of a sentence, the verb will often be omitted.

As with other instances of the particle と being used, this use simply expresses the relationship between (A) 'what was communicated', and (B) 'how it was communicated'.

attributes.source: [DBJG] A Dictionary of Basic Japanese Grammar

attributes.description: Quoting What Someone Said Using Japanese Particle と
Said in Japanese (と言った vs って言ってた)

attributes.body: と is a quoting particle used to mark the content of direct or indirect speech, thoughts, or feelings. For example, 行くと言っていた means '[He] was saying [he] will go.' といってもいい combines と with 言う and the い-Adjective いい, meaning 'You/one could say' (literally, 'It's fine even if one says...').

first_relatable.title: といってもいい
first_relatable.meaning: You could say, You might say

attributes.body: と and って are quoting particles marking direct or indirect speech, thoughts, or feelings. For example, 行くと言っていた and 行くって言っていた both mean '[They] were saying [they] will go.' The difference is that って is used mainly in casual conversation, while と is used in speech or writing. って can also casually introduce a topic, like 日本っていいよね ('Japan is great, isn't it?'), which と cannot.
